Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

cd

Change the working directory

Stata 

cd "path/to/folder"

R base 

setwd("path/to/folder")

An RStudio project sets the working directory for you, so scripts can use relative paths.

Stata reference · R reference

clear

Remove a dataset from memory

Stata 

clear

R base 

rm(data)

Rarely needed: R holds many tables at once, each under its own name.

1 more examples and alternatives

Export an Excel file

Stata reference · R reference

findit

Find the R equivalent of a Stata command

Stata 

findit command

R tidystata 

findit(command)

Bare words and comma-separated names work: findit(tab, sex, region). Add hints such as findit(tab, gen), or quote full Stata syntax. A bare command browses its whole family and shows up to five operations; a clear specific query returns one answer, and ambiguous queries retain up to ten relevant candidates. print(n = Inf) expands the returned results; use the bare command for broader family operations. Within a matching operation, recommendations prefer tidystata, then tidyverse, then other packages or base R. findit() with no argument returns the whole catalogue.

Stata reference · R reference

global

Store a value for later use

Stata 

global path "path/to/folder"

R base 

path <- "path/to/folder"

Any R object works like a macro: assign it once and reuse its name, as in setwd(path).

Stata reference · R reference

help

Open the help page of a function

Stata 

help command

R utils 

help(function_name)

?function does the same. In RStudio you can also search the Help pane.

Stata reference · R reference

import

Import a CSV file

Stata 

import delimited data.csv

R readr 

data <- readr::read_csv("data.csv")

RStudio's File > Import Dataset menu writes this code for you.

Stata reference · R reference

Stata

R readxl 

data <- readxl::read_excel("data.xlsx")

save

Save as a Stata dataset

Stata 

save data.dta, replace

R haven 

haven::write_dta(data, "data.dta")

saveRDS(data, "data.rds") keeps every R type, such as factors and dates, exactly.

Stata reference · R reference

saveold

Save for an older Stata version

Stata 

saveold data.dta, version(13)

R haven 

haven::write_dta(data, "data.dta", version = 13)

Stata reference · R reference

search

Search all installed help pages

Stata 

search keyword

R utils 

help.search("keyword")

??keyword is a shortcut. To find the R version of a Stata command, use findit().

Stata reference · R reference

ssc

Install a package

Stata 

ssc install package

R utils 

install.packages("package")

Unlike Stata, an installed package must be attached in every session with library(package).

Stata reference · R reference

sysuse

Load an example dataset

Stata 

sysuse auto

R datasets 

data("mtcars")

Stata reference · R reference

use

Open a Stata dataset

Stata 

use data.dta

R haven 

data <- haven::read_dta("data.dta")

Variable and value labels are kept. Data saved in R's own format open with readRDS("data.rds") or load("data.RData").

Stata reference · R reference

webuse

Load an example dataset from the Stata website

Stata

R haven 

data <- haven::read_dta("https://www.stata-press.com/data/r18/nlswork.dta")
